audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers read Mordekaiser for Level 6, First item and 2+ items. The packet chart reads Skill / Nasus / Nasus for those rows, the win rate is 50.19% over 746 games, and the page's own prose (whys[4] 'genuinely contested', whys[5] 'the lane is his now', late 'stop trying to solo-duel the dog') says Nasus takes over.
audit.why: A Nasus with Sheen and a few hundred Siphoning Strike stacks out-grinds Darkness Rise, and Fury of the Sands adds percent-max-HP damage plus armour and MR.
audit.corrected: Rows 4-6 flipped in BOTH layers as one atomic group: phases[4].side/win[4] -> Skill, phases[5..6].side/win[5..6] -> Nasus, with ratings 5/10, 4/10, 3/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: First-item and two-item rows were written as Mordekaiser spikes; the real second-half spike belongs to Nasus (Sheen + stack count, then Fury of the Sands).
audit.why: Siphoning Strike drops to 3.5s at rank 5 and its cooldown is reduced further inside Fury of the Sands, which also grants bonus HP, attack range, armour and MR.
audit.corrected: Morde's spikes are level 3 (full kit + Darkness Rise) and level 6 (Realm of Death, 140s at rank 1, 650 range). After that the spikes are his.

audit.whatIsWrong: Wither had no numbers, and nothing stated that Fury of the Sands invalidates flat resistances or shortens his Q cooldown inside the Realm.
audit.why: Wither: 15/14/13/12/11s, 700 range, decays move and attack speed. Fury of the Sands: percentHealth damage plus bonus armour/MR and a reduced Siphoning Strike cooldown — so the Realm 1v1 gets worse the longer you leave it.
audit.corrected: Bait Wither and commit inside its 15s downtime; take the Realm before he has stacks, because Fury of the Sands gives him more Q casts in there; do not answer him with raw armour.

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[2].d was a copy-paste of the bad-trade line and said nothing about scaling.
audit.why: The don't is titled 'Let him scale to lategame'; the body did not address it.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the Fury of the Sands resistance point.

edits.before: Realm of Death online — the 1v1 Nasus cannot decline. R steals 10% of his stats; take the duel whenever Wither is down and the wave is shoved.
edits.after: Realm of Death online — a 1v1 Nasus cannot decline, but his stacks climb every wave: take the duel while Wither's 15s is down, and take it early.

edits.before: Liandry's makes Darkness Rise melt through bruiser HP stacking. Extended trades are now strictly yours — force them.
edits.after: Sheen and a few hundred stacks flip it — Siphoning Strike shreds through Indestructible and out-grinds your aura.

edits.before: Riftmaker omnivamp turns the Realm 1v1 unloseable into most matchups. Nasus's only outs are dodging Q forever or never being alone — neither survives a whole game.
edits.after: Fury of the Sands adds percent-max-HP damage plus armour and MR, so stacking resistances is the wrong answer — stop dueling him and group with your team.

edits.before: - Nasus Wither: matchup-defining — His only kite. Bait it before R. Track it before every engage.
edits.after: - Nasus Wither (W): matchup-defining — 15s at rank 1, 700 range. Bait it, then engage inside that window.

edits.before: His only kite. Bait it before R. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Wither (W) is 15s at rank 1. Bait it, then commit inside that window.

edits.before: Burning your answer for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Wither guts move and attack speed — disengage and re-enter when its 15s is up.

edits.before: Whiffing Q into the wave and trading with no passive stacks — un-isolated Obliterate hits soft, and without Darkness Rise you lose most even exchanges.
edits.after: Fury of the Sands scales on max HP and hands him armour and MR — flat resistances are no answer, so end the game before he cashes his stacks.

edits.before: Realm of Death banishes him into a 1v1 with no minions to Q-stack and no jungler to peel — the cleanest kill window you'll get all game.
edits.after: Realm of Death banishes him with no minions to Q-stack — but Fury of the Sands cuts his Q cooldown inside, so take the duel before he has stacks.

notes: suspectNames flagged 'Use Death's Grasp' in wants.you[2] — FALSE POSITIVE, Death's Grasp is Mordekaiser's own E. Real defect was the level chart: both layers read Mordekaiser for Level 6 / First item / 2+ items while the packet chart, the 50.19% win rate and the page's own late-game prose all say Nasus takes over. Rows 4-6 are proposed as one atomic paired group (full phases[N].side + content win[N] together). Kit-data warning confirmed from the mirror: Mordekaiser Q is flagged 'grounding' only because its text says 'smashes the ground' — Obliterate does not ground, so no page text asserts it.
